title: Who was Cesar Virata?
summary: Cesar E.A. Virata, the Philippines" longest-serving finance chief and prime minister under President Ferdinand Marcos Sr., passed away on Friday, October 2, at the age of 95.
byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Cesar E.A. Virata, the Philippines’ longest-serving finance chief and prime minister under President Ferdinand Marcos Sr., passed away on Friday, October 2, at the age of 95.
Virata served as finance secretary from 1970 to 1978 and finance minister from 1978 to 1986.
He was the Philippines’ prime minister from 1981 to 1986. He also served as the country’s governor at the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.
As a key figure in economic policymaking, Virata was recognized by the Department of Finance (DOF), among other former secretaries, for his leadership during major crises.
He was at the helm of the DOF when Super Typhoon Yoling and the Great Central Luzon Flood struck the country in 1970.
His death was announced by the Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC), where he served as a director since 1995 and as corporate vice chairperson for 26 years.

Virata was also a longtime educator at the University of the Philippines (UP), where he served as dean of the UP College of Business Administration from 1960 to 1967 and is credited with introducing the Master of Business Administration program.

He graduated cum laude from UP with degrees in Mechanical Engineering and Business Administration before earning a Master of Business Administration in Industrial Management from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania.

A biography of Virata, “Cesar Virata: Life and Times Through Four Decades of Philippine Economic History,“ was launched in 2014 by economist and educator Gerardo Sicat after 12 years of research and writing.

“He covered all aspects of the tax system – national and local, and also international taxation. His contributions are beyond tax changes. Many of these were in the nature of administrative decisions as well as the infusion of delicate rules and protocols of tax reviews and investigations,” Sicat said in a paper released in 2011.
Virata’s career in government and academe spanned several decades, making him one of the Philippines’ most prominent economic managers of the postwar era. —VAL, GMA News
